 Order
Petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order dated 7/4/2023, whereby, he was dismissed from service on account of his conviction in a criminal case.
The petitioner has also challenged the order dated 19/1/2024, whereby, the appeal filed by him against the order of punishment has been dismissed by the appellate authority.
2. The facts necessary for decision of this case are that the petitioner's father, late Shri Siyaram Singh Baghel, was working in the Police Department.
He died in harness in year 2006.
The petitioner was granted appointment on compassionate ground in year 2007 on the post of Constable.
At the relevant time, he was posted in Police Line, Bhind.
3. It is pertinent to note here that prior to his compassionate appointment, the petitioner was the Director of a Company namely Pravachan Dairies and Allied Limited.
He tendered his resignation from the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 2 WP-27321-2024 directorship of the company on 20/8/2006 before taking up the compassionate appointment.

4. While working as Constable in Police Line, Bhind, a criminal case was registered against the petitioner at Gole Ka Mandir Police Station, Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 420 of IPC, Section 3(1)(2) (4) of Madhya Pradesh Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000 and Section 45-S, 58-B and 5-A of Reserve Bank of India Act and Section 4,5,6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978.

sentences.text: The petitioner has challenged his conviction before this Court in Criminal Appeal No.157/2022, which is stated to be pending.
The sentence of the petitioner has been suspended by this Court.

6. As a result of petitioner's conviction in the aforesaid case, the respondent/authority issued a show cause notice to the petitioner on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 3 WP-27321-2024 20/3/2023 proposing action under Regular 238 of Police Regulations.
The petitioner submitted his reply to the show cause notice.
Thereafter, the impugned order is passed by respondent no.4, whereby, petitioner has been dismissed from service in exercise of powers under Regular 238 of M.P. Police Regulations.
Being aggrieved, petitioner challenged the punishment order before respondent no.3, which also suffered dismissal vide impugned order dated 19/1/2024 (Annexure P/2).
Challenging these two orders, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.

7. Challenging the impugned orders, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that the petitioner was convicted for a petty offence under Section 3(4) of Adhiniyam, 2000 for which he is inflicted with imprisonment of only three months RI, and therefore, looking to the nature of offence, the punishment of dismissal from service is unduly harsh and disproportionate.
It is his submission that impugned order of punishment has been passed merely because the petitioner has been convicted in criminal case without considering the nature and gravity of the offence.

The learned counsel submitted that Regulation 238 of the Police Regulations provides discretion to the Inspector General of Police to allow retention of a member in force, if the offence was not serious or disgraceful in nature and the imprisonment was not so prolonged.
It is his submission that the authorities failed to properly exercise the powers under Regulation 238 and mechanically imposed the punishment of dismissal from service.

In support of his submission, learned counsel relied upon the Apex Court decision in the case of State of M.P. & Ors. Vs. Hazarilal, reported in (2008)3 SCC 273 as also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 4 WP-27321-2024 Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Tikaram Windwar Vs. Registrar, Co-operative Societies, M.P.,
Bhopal & Ors., reported in 1977 SCC Online MP 66.
8.

It is his submission that respondent/authorities were justified in inflicting punishment of dismissal from service.

He placed reliance upon Full Bench decision of this Court in the case of Laxmi Narayan Hayaran Vs. State of M.P. & Anr., reported in 2004(4) MPLJ 555.

sentences.text: Before adverting to the facts of the case, the provisions of Regulation 238 of Police Regulations needs to be examined.

Regulation 238 of Police Regulations provides as under:-
"238. Conviction in criminal offence.- When a Police officer has bee sentenced by the Trial court to rigorous imprisonment upon conviction of a criminal offence, he shall be dismissed from the force:
Provided that if his offence was not of a serious or disgraceful nature, and the imprisonment has not been so prolonged as to be of it self degrading, it shall be in the discretion of the Inspector- General to allow is retention in the force."
11.

A perusal of the proviso makes it evident that if the offence for which a member of force is convicted is not of serious or disgraceful nature and the imprisonment has not been prolonged, the Inspector- General of Police may allow his retention in the force.

Thus, while exercising powers NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 5 WP-27321-2024 under Regulation 238, the authorities were required to consider the act alleged against the petitioner as also the nature of offence in question.
The period of sentence is also of relevant consideration.

12. The similar provision is made in Rule 19 of M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal)
Rules, 1966 which provides as under:-
"19. Special procedure in certain cases:- Notwithstanding anything contained in rule 14 to rule 18:-
(i) where any penalty is imposed on a Government servant on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge, or (ii) where the disciplinary authority is satisfied for reasons to be recorded by it in writing that it is not reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry in the manner provided in these rules, or (iii) where the Governor is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State, it is not expedient to hold any inquiry in the manner provided in these rules, the disciplinary authority may consider the circumstances of the case and make such orders thereon as it deems fit:
Provided further that the Commission shall be consulted where such consultation is necessary, before any orders are made in any case under this rule.

sentences.text: 13. The aforesaid provision of Rule 19 of CCA Rules, was considered by the Apex Court in the case of Hazarilal (supra) .

The Court, after referring to Rule 19 of CCA Rules, held in para 7 & 8 as under:-
"7.

By reason of the said provision, thus, "the disciplinary authority has been empowered to consider the circumstances of the case where any penalty is imposed Kamal Singh Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151065993/
3 on a government servant on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge", but the same would not mean that irrespective of the nature of the case in which he was involved or the punishment which has been imposed upon him,
an order of dismissal must be passed.

entities.text: Kamal Singh Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such a construction, in our opinion, is not warranted.

8. An authority which is conferred with a statutory discretionary power is bound to take into consideration all the attending facts NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 6 WP-27321-2024 and circumstances of the case before imposing an order of punishment.
While exercising such power, the disciplinary authority must act reasonably and fairly.
The respondent occupied the lowest rank of the cadre.
He was merely a contingency peon.
Continuation of his service in the department would not bring a bad name to the State.
He was not convicted for any act involving moral turpitude.
He was not punished for any heinous offence."
14. The Division Bench of this Court in the case of Tikaram Windwar (supra) has also considered the provision of Rule 19 of CCA Rules.

The Division Bench held as under:-
"Rule 19 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal)
Rules must bear the same construction as was put upon Rule 14 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules by the Supreme Court in Challappan's case.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, even in a case where penalty is imposed on a Government employee on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge, there should be a summary inquiry after noticing the Government employee concerned in the way pointed out by the Supreme Court in Challappan's case.
Conviction on a criminal charge does not necessarily mean that the employee concerned should be removed or dismissed from service.
The nature of penalty will naturally depend upon the gravity of the offence for which the employee is convicted.

It is, therefore, necessary for the disciplinary authority to decide even in such cases whether in the facts and circumstances of a particular case, what penalty, if at all, should be imposed on the delinquent employee.
In determining this question, the delinquent employee should be noticed to put forward his point of view and the circumstances of the case why no penalty or a lesser penalty should be imposed on him.
As in the instant case no inquiry was at all held, the order of dismissal cannot be sustained."

15. Even though the law laid down by Division Bench in the aforesaid case that the delinquent is required to be noticed before inflicting punishment under Rule 19 CCA Rules is overruled by Full Bench of this Court in the case of Laxmi Narayan Hayaran (supra), the law regarding NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 7 WP-27321-2024 consideration of facts before inflicting punishment is affirmed by Full Bench.

16. Considering the aforesaid, it is clear that while taking action against the delinquent, based upon his conviction in a criminal case, the authority is required to consider the facts of the case including the gravity of offence for which employee is convicted, before imposing any punishment.

In other Kamal Singh Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151065993/
4 words, it is not a thumb-rule that in every case of conviction, the extreme punishment of dismissal is to be imposed irrespective of gravity of offence.

sentences.text: The action of the disciplinary authority must be reasonable and fair.

17. Keeping in view aforesaid legal position, if the facts of the present case are seen, it is gathered that the petitioner is convicted and sentenced to suffer three months RI with fine of Rs. 1,000/-.

When the immpugned orders passed by respondents no.3 & 4 are meticulously examined, it is gathered that after referring to the facts of the case, the impugned action is directed against the petitioner without even discussing the facts of criminal case as also the gravity of offence for which petitioner is convicted and sentenced.
For ready reference, concluding paragraph of the impugned order passed by respondent no.4 is reproduced hereunder:-

Similar is the case with the appellate order passed by respondent no.3, wherein, the appellate a u t h o r i t y a f t e r r e p r o d u c i n g t h e f a c t s o f t h e c a s e , N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 8 WP-27321-2024
ultimately in four lines, dismissed the appeal and closed the matter.
Thus, both the authorities miserably failed to properly exercise the powers under Regulation 238 inasmuch as they did not even advert to the facts of the criminal case.

19. While taking action against an incumbent on account of his conviction, various aspects are required to be looked into viz. (i) post held by the incumbent; (ii) nature of offence alleged; and (iii)
longevity of sentence imposed and the time gap between the date of alleged offence and the action being taken etc.

Both the authorities i.e. respondents no.3 & 4 have failed to consider any of the aforesaid facts of the case and have mechanically passed impugned orders inflicting punishment of dismissal from service.
20. The issue involving interpretation of Rule 19 of CCA Rules has been considered by this Court in cases more than once.

In the case o f Mahima Chand Gangwar Vs. State of M.P. & Ors., reported in 2016(2) MPLJ 403, the petitioner was a Upper Division Teacher in Govt. School who was convicted for offence under Section 324/34 of IPC and was imposed with sentence of two years RI.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court interfered in the matter holding that the punishment of dismissal is disproportionate.

21. In another case of Dinesh Kumar Bilthare Vs. State of M.P. & Ors., reported in 2024(1) MPLJ 339, while dealing with a case of Teacher, who was convicted for offence under Section 324 of IPC and sentenced to suffered six months RI with fine of Rs.1,000/-, this Court held in para 11 as under:-

sentences.text: If the impugned order dated 27-11-2020 (Annexure P-6) is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 9 WP-27321-2024 minutely examined, it will be clear like cloudless sky that there is no iota of reason assigned in the entire order as to why the punishment of 'removal' from service was found to be adequate for committing the offence under section 324 of Penal Code, 1860.
The disciplinary authority was required to examine the gravity of conduct which led to conviction on the principles of proportionality.
There is no finding that the conduct which led to conviction was so grave that no such other punishment would be commensurate to the offence/conduct.
Thus, the order dated 27- 11-2010 is set aside.

The District Education Officer, Chhatarpur is directed to re-consider the punishment on the anvil of doctrine of proportionality and pass a fresh order in accordance with law within 30 days from the date of production of copy of this order."
22.

Similar view was taken by this Court in the case of Vijay Kumar Tiwari Vs. State of M.P. & Ors.,
reported in 2024 SCC Online MP 5468 , wherein also, the delinquent was convicted for offence under Section 324/34 of IPC and sentenced to suffer RI for six months with fine of Rs. 300/-.
23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In all the aforesaid cases, this Court has held that the authorities have failed to consider relevant facts while imposing punishment of dismissal.
Looking to the nature of offence, in all the aforesaid cases, this Court has held that the punishment of dismissal from service is disproportionate.
24. In the instant case also, the offence alleged against the petitioner relates back to the period when he was Director of Pravachan Dairies and Allied Limited Company.
Meaning thereby, the offence alleged against him was not committed by the petitioner during the course of his employment with the respondent/department.
The act alleged relates back to period prior to the year 2006 of which the action is being taken in year 2023.
Further, the punishment of 3 months RI only has been inflicted upon the petitioner.

Thus, the punishment of dismissal from service is found to be unduly harsh and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 10 WP-27321-2024 disproportionate to the offence alleged against the petitioner.
The respondent/authorities have failed to consider the relevant aspects of the matter while imposing impugned punishment.

25. As regards decision of the Full Bench of this Court in the case o f Laxmi Narayan Hayaran (supra), as relied upon by the State counsel to support the impugned action of the respondents, it is gathered that the Full Bench was primarily considering the issue as to whether while imposing the punishment under Rule 19 of CCA Rules, an opportunity of hearing is required to be given to the delinquent or not.
The Full Bench answered the issue in negative in its judgment.

The Full Bench held in para 10 to 12 as under:-
"10. Rule 19 of the State CCA Rules is similar to Rule 14 of Railway Rules considered in Challappan (supra) and unamended Rule 19 of Central CCA Rules considered in Tulsiram Patel, which did not provide for any opportunity of hearing in regard to the penalty to be imposed.
In Tulsiram Patel (supra), the Supreme Court has categorically held that no opportunity need be given to the employee concerned, but the disciplinary authority

, on consideration of the facts and circumstances (in the Kamal Singh Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151065993/
6 manner set out in Challappan and Tulsiram Patel)

entities.text: Kamal Singh Baghel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: may impose the penalty.
It was also clarified that if the penalty imposed was whimsical or disproportionately excessive, the same was open to correction in judicial review.
The subsequent decision of the Supreme Court in Sunil Kumar Sarkar (supra) dealt with the amended Rule 19 of the Central CCA Rules which provided for a hearing.

Therefore, the principle laid down in Sunil Kumar Sarkar (supra) cannot be of any assistance in interpreting Rule 19 of the State CCA Rules in the absence of an amendment in the State CCA Rules corresponding to the amendment made in the Central CCA Rules.
As the State CCA Rules stand today, the law applicable is as laid down in Tulsiram Patel (supra) and not as laid down in Sunil Kumar Sarkar.

11. We accordingly overrule the decisions of the Division Bench NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 11 WP-27321-2024 in Tikaram (supra) and Sheetal Kumar Bandi (supra), insofar as they hold that the delinquent employee should be given a notice giving an opportunity to put forth his views as to the penalty proposed to be imposed.

12. The second premise in the Sheetal Kumar Bandi (supra) that in exercise of the power of judicial review, the Court can examine whether there was consideration of the relevant facts and circumstances by the disciplinary authority in imposing the penalty and correct the penalty if it is excessive, is in consonance with the decisions of the Supreme Court in Challappan, Shankar Dass, Tulsiram Patel and Sunil Kumar Sarkar (supra).
If the conviction is for any minor offence which does not involve any moral turpitude, a punishment of removal or dismissal from service will certainly be excessive.

But where the conviction is on the ground of corruption, as in this case,
there can be no two views that imposition of punishment by way of dismissal is just and proper and not excessive."
26.

Thus, even the Full Bench of this Court in the case of Laxmi Narayan Hayaran (supra) has held that the competent authority is required to consider the fact of each case while taking action under Rule 19 of CCA Rules and the punishment of dismissal from services cannot be mechanically passed in all cases.

27. In view of the discussion made above, this Court is of the view that the punishment imposed upon the petitioner vide impugned orders is harsh and disproportionate to the gravity of offence committed by the petitioner.
The impugned orders dated 7/4/2023 (Annexure P/1) and 19/1/2024 (Annexure P/2) are therefore, quashed.
The respondents are directed to reinstate the petitioner in service.
The matter is remitted to respondent no.4 for reconsideration of the matter afresh for purposes of imposing punishment on the petitioner keeping in view the aforesaid observations of this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:25263 12 WP-27321-2024 28.
The petition stands allowed and disposed of, accordingly.
